source_text: The one-line gray message is better, thanks.  What I'm thinking now is that we should put our heads together with codex-10 who has been doing excellent work on the War Machine side.  I think we'd increasingly be in a position to work on the "close AIF over the operator" material: from the M-象-2000 side we now have tool, and from the AIF side the theory now finally seems to have a viable implementation.  I'm not saying we should embark on coding that up right now, but we could try to "zip" the two sides to form a mission... maybe we could even work on the mission from both sides, swapping work between the automated team and the interactive session team.

reply_text:
㊥ Gist: I've started a mission draft, `futon3c/holes/missions/M-aif-over-the-operator.md` (commit 64808cdc), and asked codex-10 to fill in the War Machine half. I wrote the interactive half from what exists today: offers, agreements, refusals, withdrawals and turn evidence. Once codex-10 replies, I'll draft the section that joins the two halves and show it to you. No code is involved, only writing.

㊢ (what the draft holds)
- **Origin:** your words today, plus the problem as `sec-operator.tex` states it. The 108 unanswered proposals in WR-0 couldn't tell rejection from absence. The paper's remedy is to record accepted, declined and no-response separately.
- **Side A, the interactive side (mine):** the records that are live now, and what each offer can give an AIF loop: accepted (which option), declined, withdrawn, or expired with no response, with your turn as the basis.
- **Side A gaps:**
  - a 🈸 in an agent's reply doesn't post an offer, so most asks leave no record;
  - there's no fixed-string form for declining, since only "yes" is parsed;
  - War Machine notifications (nag, brief, silent) aren't offers, so the WR-0 case would still go unrecorded.
- **Side B, the War Machine side:** left for codex-10. It asks what the AIF implementation computes live, where an observation of your responses would enter and what it would update, and how that differs from what the War Machine already learns from, such as picking a new pattern to get unstuck.
- **The join, and how to split the work between the teams:** marked as open, with one candidate split. The interactive side posts and answers offers and spots new items in dialogue. The automated side turns the recorded outcomes into credit and a proposal policy.

㊢ (the handoff)
- **Job:** `invoke-1790873058224-29744-663ef2c1`, in work mode. It's running, and codex-10 was idle beforehand.
- **Park:** `park-3492499f-c575-4a1b-bbca-4c942733f338`, with a 45-minute deadline. When codex-10 bells back, I'll check its sha and the files it cites, then write the join.

㊟ (one thing I couldn't confirm) I don't know where 象's readings of your turns are stored durably. The draft marks that as "to confirm" rather than guessing.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: Gist: The outcome of a yes is now one dim, indented line with short ids, for example `✓ agreed: option 2 of act:31e3fc8d (agreement act:32ab1363)`. There's no "system:" name, no blank line after it, and no "agreement only, no grant", since the next turn's header already gives the full ids and says that. It's loaded in your Emacs and committed (60e214e1). To check it rendered, I inserted one sample line for the agreement you just made, so you'll see it once above your prompt.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(the other forms) A refusal or failure gets the same dim style:
- `? yes was ambiguous; the agent will ask which`
- `✗ yes not recorded: withdrawn`
- `✗ yes not checked: http 403, evidence-not-operator-turn`
- `✗ yes not checked: timeout`

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (what I checked) The agent-chat ERT tests pass, 57 of 57. I updated the expected strings and added one test that the line is a single shadow-face line with shortened ids and no "system:" prefix. In your buffer, the sample line has the `shadow` face.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (what I didn't change) Only the acceptance lines changed. agent-chat.el has about 20 other places that print a full "system:" message, including the undo line. If you want those quieter too, `agent-chat--insert-note` is the function they could switch to, one at a time.
